correctness.rationale: Explicit spherical Hankel formulas yield a rational phase R_l at every nonzero j_l zero. Coprimality follows from the nonvanishing Wronskian. The pole counts and 1/z asymptotic jointly force an identity R_l^a=R_m((a/b)z)^b only when l=m=0 or l=m>0,a=b. A common zero outside those cases is algebraic as the root of a nonzero polynomial, contradicting Lindemann–Weierstrass since e^(2ix)=R_l(x) would then be algebraic. Both exceptional cases have real zeros. Exact finite symbolic checks cover representative formulas without substituting for the universal reasoning.

value.rationale: The statement is a natural complete classification of exact radial spectral collisions across all angular momenta under rational radial rescaling. It resolves the different-order case omitted by fixed-order noncommensurability and by unscaled Bourget rigidity; pole-count matches alone allow candidate scaled resonances (e.g., orders 1 and 2 at scale 2), and the subleading phase term eliminates them. The classification is not an arbitrary finite computation and has direct relevance to multi-order Fourier–Bessel spectral identifiability. It asserts no quantitative separation.
